trace: GraphRecord is canonical in packages/core/models.py. It stores body content plus provenance, trust, sensitivity, freshness, admission, eligibility, agent origin, export grant, tags, and sequence.

Public export calls export_graph. It requires an enabled ExportPolicy, known requested IDs, item-level export_allowed, authenticated eligibility, and complete exported edge endpoints. Records serialize through to_pointer_dict, so content is omitted.

Serialized graph projection calls select first, then serialize_projection. select compares full and authenticated projections. Any record-ID divergence returns fail_closed with empty records and edges. The serializer emits graph-projection-v1 with pointer records and eligible endpoint-contained edges.

serialize_projection itself trusts SelectionResult and does not re-check export_allowed. The normal select path enforces sensitivity and authentication, but a fabricated SelectionResult could bypass that assumption.

privacy_boundary.public_export: Default deny. ExportPolicy defaults to disabled and public sensitivity. A caller can explicitly broaden allowed_sensitivities.
privacy_boundary.authenticated_selection: Requires eligible, verified provenance, allowed trust, current freshness, permitted sensitivity, and policy/verifier admission. Agent-generated records also require policy-admitted trust plus verifier admission.
privacy_boundary.content_boundary: Graph exports and graph projections preserve pointers and evidence metadata, not GraphRecord.content. select_documents is a separate graph-source-context-v2 path that can include exact verified source content.

preserved_evidence: Record ID, kind, title, provenance path, SHA-256, locator, verification flag, trust, sensitivity, freshness, admission, eligibility, agent-generated flag, export grant, tags, and sequence.
Edges preserve IDs, endpoints, relation, relevance, provenance, trust, sensitivity, freshness, admission, eligibility, agent origin, and export grant.
Projection envelopes preserve task ID, topology, fail-closed state, reason, and divergent IDs.
budget_behavior: TaskSpec defaults to max_depth=4, node_budget=200, and byte_budget=32768.
Selection caps seeds and graph expansion at node_budget and stops at max_depth.
Serialization uses deterministic topology ordering, then removes the last record until canonical JSON fits byte_budget. Edges whose endpoints are removed are also removed.
Fail-closed envelopes must fit the byte budget; otherwise serialization raises. Public export has no node or byte budget.
answer.canonical_ownership: packages/core and contracts/core are canonical. plugins/graph-engineering/runtime is generated. contracts/package/projection-map.json maps canonical sources to runtime targets and excludes four historical V3 routing schemas. The graph remains a derived view and does not replace cited source truth.
package_drift_checks: The projector validates normalized relative paths, non-overlapping mappings, approved exclusions, symlink and regular-file safety, and exact prior projection state before replacing runtime content.

The parity verifier compares canonical mapped bytes with runtime bytes, checks runtime file-set equality, validates projection-state schema and contract digest, and checks recorded file sizes and SHA-256 values.

Release verification rebuilds the package inventory, validates plugin name/version, and rejects missing, extra, changed, duplicate, escaping, private or machine-specific, symlink, hard-link, oversized, and non-regular entries. A mismatch returns source_package_drift.
answer.proof_boundary: This is source-trace evidence only. No benchmark artifact, graph-find command, parity checker, runtime export, installation, or publication proof was used.
